native_result.query: What kind of demographic disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated?
native_result.HypoA: Gender disparities exist in median wealth in 1985 among individuals who were ever incarcerated, with males having higher median wealth than females.
native_result.HypoB: Among NLSY79 respondents who were ever incarcerated (ever_jailed == 1, n = 289), median 1985 wealth — measured at or before incarceration onset, since ever_jailed covers jailings in 1985–1994 — is only $720 versus $3,600 for never-incarcerated peers. Within the ever-incarcerated group: (1) race disparity among jailed men — White men's median wealth ($2,000) is ~2.5× Black men's ($800) and ~2.9× Hispanic men's ($700); (2) sex disparity — jailed women's median wealth is $0 versus $1,000 for jailed men, with 65% of jailed women (vs 36% of jailed men) at zero or negative net worth; (3) the incarcerated are worse off than never-incarcerated peers of the same race and sex in every cell, but the dollar gap is largest for Hispanic men (−$4,300) and White men (−$3,500) and smallest for Black men (−$700), whose never-jailed peers already have low median wealth ($1,500) — indicating racial wealth disparities precede and compound with incarceration. Subgroup medians for jailed women (Black $0 n=16, Hispanic $0 n=9, White $4,100 n=12) are reported but unstable given n=9–16. Data-grounded: all figures from median/zero-share tables in outputs/.
